reasons: The document genuinely lacks any operative indemnity: Section 7 (p0034-p0037) contains only liability caps and an attorneys' fees waiver despite its 'Indemnification of Contractor' caption, and the only IP protection (p0026) is a bare non-infringement warranty with no defence obligation — this is walk-away territory ('no Vendor IP indemnity at all'), so 'missing' is correctly classified.

The inserted Section 7(d) tracks the playbook's model language (IP infringement, breach of law, Contractor-caused data incidents, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) with standard notice/control/cooperation mechanics, and is placed as an addition after the limitation-of-liability paragraph exactly as the redline guidance directs.

The carve-out from the Section 7(a) fees-paid cap and the Section 7(c) fees waiver is necessary rather than over-reaching — without it the defence obligation would be neutralised — and it does not duplicate a separate liability-cap flag because it is scoped only to the new indemnity.

No Customer indemnity exists, so there is nothing to narrow on our side; the comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice, explains the change and offers the fallback (IP-only indemnity with modification/combination exclusions and 3x annual fees super-cap) as a landing zone.

Deterministic checks confirm the operation applies and the vendor IP indemnity language is present; only trivial imprecision (paraphrased section caption, unverifiable Paragraph 9 aside) which does not affect the substance.
